Render One Report Template for Several Variants of Its Parameters

Source: R/render_variants.R
render_variants.Rd

Renders a single parameterized Quarto (or R Markdown) report once per variant, so that analyses which differ only in a choice (for example the original data and the imputed data, use_imputed = FALSE / TRUE) are produced from one canonical template instead of from copies that drift apart. Each variant is a named list of parameters; the output files are named <template>_<variant>.<extension>.

Usage

render_variants(
  input,
  variants,
  formats = "html",
  output_dir = NULL,
  stop_on_error = TRUE,
  dry_run = FALSE,
  self_contained = TRUE,
  check_params = TRUE,
  renderer = NULL,
  quiet = TRUE
)

Arguments

input

Path to the .qmd or .Rmd template.

variants

A named list; each element is a named list of parameters for one rendering, for example list(original = list(use_imputed = FALSE), imputed = list(use_imputed = TRUE)). Names must be unique and consist of letters, digits, _, . or -.

formats

Output formats to render for each variant (default "html"), for example c("html", "docx"). Letters, digits, _ and - only.

output_dir

Folder for the outputs. Defaults to the folder of the template.

stop_on_error

If TRUE (default), the first failed rendering stops the run with an error of class render_variants_error that carries the results so far in $results; if FALSE, failures are recorded in the result and the other variants are still rendered.

dry_run

If TRUE, nothing is rendered; the plan is returned.

self_contained

For .qmd HTML output, ask for one self-contained file; see Details. Default TRUE.

check_params

If TRUE (default), check the variants' parameters against the template's params:; see Details.

renderer

The function that renders one document, with the arguments of quarto::quarto_render() (input, output_format, output_file, execute_params, quiet, metadata). Defaults to quarto::quarto_render for a .qmd and to rmarkdown::render (with params) for an .Rmd.

quiet

Passed on to the renderer.

Value

A tibble with one row per variant and format: variant, format, params (a list column), output (the final file), status ("rendered", "failed" or "planned") and error.

Details

Parameters are checked. Every parameter a variant sets must be declared under params: in the template's YAML header: a misspelled parameter is an error before anything is rendered (Quarto would otherwise ignore it and silently render the default). The keys are read from the header as written, so parameters such as n, y or on are not mistaken for YAML booleans. A parameter that no variant sets keeps the template's default. The check is skipped, with a warning, when the header cannot be read; check_params = FALSE switches it off (needed for a Jupyter notebook template whose parameters are declared in a parameters-tagged cell).

Your files are not touched. Each rendering is written to a file with a private name in the template's folder and then renamed or moved to its final name, so a file that already exists next to the template (a hand-made analysis_final.html, say) is never overwritten, moved or deleted. A file at the final name in output_dir is replaced. The private file is removed if the rendering fails.

HTML. Quarto's default HTML needs a folder of support files named after the template, shared by every variant and not moved with the output. self_contained = TRUE (default) therefore asks for a single self-contained HTML file (embed-resources: true); with FALSE you must keep the support folder yourself and variants overwrite each other's figures. For an R Markdown template the setting is not applied (html_document is self-contained by default).

See also

[render_pipeline()], [extract_yaml_formats()]

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
render_variants(
  "analysis/single_var_mixed_models.qmd",
  variants = list(original = list(use_imputed = FALSE), imputed = list(use_imputed = TRUE)),
  formats = c("html", "docx"),
  output_dir = "reports"
)
} # }
